label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 15
knowledgePattern: Compose a supplied fractional-part function and count verified integer branches
solution:
For any real u and integer m, {u−m}={u}. Since {2x}+{3x}=5x−⌊2x⌋−⌊3x⌋, taking the fractional part gives f(x)={5x}. Composing again gives f(f(x))={5{5x}}={25x}.

For 0≤x<1, let k=⌊25x⌋, so k is one of the integers 0 to 24. The equation becomes 25x−k=1−x, giving x=(k+1)/26.

This candidate belongs to its claimed branch precisely when k≤25(k+1)/26<k+1. The first inequality is equivalent to k≤25 and the second to k>−1, so every integer from 0 to 24 works. The resulting inputs are 1/26,2/26,…,25/26, all distinct and inside the required interval. There are 25 solutions: answer D.

hints.title: Separate the integer parts
hints.body: Replace each inner fractional part by its input minus an integer. Then take the outer fractional part: subtracting an integer does not change it.
hints.recap: Fractional part means the amount left after removing a whole-number part.
hints.pitfall: The outer braces must still be applied.
hints.pause: Simplify f, then simplify f composed with itself.

hints.title: Name the whole-number part
hints.body: For your simplified expression, let k be the integer removed by the fractional-part operation. Write the equation using k, together with the two inequalities that define that integer part.
hints.recap: A floor value k means the original number lies from k inclusive to k plus 1 exclusive.
hints.pause: Solve for x in terms of k and determine the possible integers.

hints.title: Check each case
hints.body: Substitute your expression for x back into the two inequalities for its case. Count only the integer values for which the candidate really stays in that case.
hints.recap: A candidate from a case equation must satisfy that case’s restrictions.
hints.pitfall: Count different x values, not just formal integer labels.

recall.reminder: A candidate from a case equation must satisfy that case’s restrictions.
